context.analysis:
## Overview
The system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually migrating claim types from a 30-year-old legacy mainframe to a cloud-native architecture over a three-year period. It ensures seamless online submissions for customers and brokers while maintaining business continuity through a hybrid operational model.

## Key Elements
* Policyholders (Customers) and Brokers
* Claims Adjusters
* Modern Claims Platform (Azure West Europe)
* Legacy Mainframe System of Record (COBOL/DB2 on-premise)
* Insurer Active Directory / Entra ID
* Enterprise Notification System
* Azure Service Bus

## Relationships
* Policyholders & Brokers -> Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) for online claim submissions (R-01)
* Claims Adjusters -> Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS for claim handling (R-02)
* Modern Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe: Hybrid VPN, mTLS, and Azure Service Bus for claim type migration and dual-run sync (R-03, R-04)
* Modern Claims Platform -> Insurer Active Directory: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 for Single Sign-On (R-07)
* Modern Claims Platform -> Enterprise Notification System: HTTPS/SMTP for claim status updates (R-01)

## Technology Stack
* Azure App Service / Kubernetes & .NET/Java: Hosts the modern cloud platform in West Europe for scalability and performance.
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronously decouples systems to protect the rigid nightly batch window and mainframe latency.
* Azure Key Vault with Managed Identities: Secures credentials and prevents hardcoding, mitigating cloud inexperience risks.
* Azure Bicep: Enforces Infrastructure-as-Code to minimize deployment human errors.
* Azure Monitor / Application Insights: Provides centralized distributed tracing and business-driven observability for state parity and R-06 rollbacks.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while empowering an inexperienced cloud team with robust managed Azure services. It guarantees zero data loss, strict security boundaries, and rapid rollback capabilities during the three-year incremental migration.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe by gradually migrating claims processing to a hybrid Azure cloud platform. It ensures business continuity by maintaining the legacy system of record while introducing modern web applications and event-driven microservices.]

## Key Elements
* Policyholders and Brokers (Users)
* Claims Adjusters (Users)
* API Gateway (Azure Front Door / Azure API Management)
* Claims Web Application (React / Azure App Service)
* Audit & Reporting Dashboard (React / Azure App Service)
* Claims Core Service (Node.js/TypeScript on Azure Container Apps)
* Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sync Worker (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions / .NET)
* Legacy Mainframe System (COBOL / DB2)
* Identity Provider (Azure AD / Entra ID)

## Relationships
* Policyholders/Brokers to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST (Online claim submission)
* Claims Adjusters to Claims Web Application via HTTPS/REST (Claim handling)
* API Gateway to Claims Core Service via gRPC / HTTPS (Dynamic routing)
* Claims Core Service to Legacy Mainframe via MQ/AMQP and mTLS over IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute (Hybrid data sync)
* Claims Core Service to Azure Service Bus via AMQP (Event streaming)
* Web Applications to Azure AD / Entra ID via OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 (SSO)

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Provider: Hybrid (On-premise mainframe and Azure West Europe)
* Frontend: React hosted on Azure App Service for fast adjuster UI rendering (<2s)
* Backend: Node.js/TypeScript on Azure Container Apps using CQRS and Event Sourcing
* Messaging: Azure Service Bus for standardized, managed event streaming and queuing
* Database & Caching: Azure SQL / Cosmos DB for local read models bypassing mainframe latency
* Security & Auth: Azure AD / Entra ID (OIDC), Azure Key Vault (CMK), and WAF

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples the responsive modern cloud UI from slow legacy mainframe responses using CQRS and local read models, meeting strict performance and consistency goals. Utilizing fully managed Azure services mitigates the team's low cloud experience while enabling claim-by-claim migration with rapid 1-day fallback capabilities.]

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a modern insurance claims platform API Gateway that unifies hybrid routing between a new Azure-hosted service and a legacy mainframe. Its core purpose is to securely manage external traffic while enabling gradual, zero-loss claim type migration.]

## Key Elements
* Azure Front Door / Azure API Management (API Gateway container)
* Authentication & WAF Component (APIM Policies)
* Routing Configuration Loader (Azure App Configuration)
* Transformation & Caching Component (APIM Liquid Templates / Response Cache)
* Circuit Breaker Policy Engine (APIM native policies)
* Azure Key Vault
* Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
* Policyholders and Brokers -> API Gateway: Online claim submission [HTTPS/REST via TLS 1.3]
* API Gateway -> Claims Core Service: Dynamic routing of requests [gRPC / HTTPS with mTLS]
* API Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe Proxy: Fallback routing [HTTPS with mTLS]
* API Gateway -> Azure App Configuration: Fetch routing definitions [HTTPS]
* API Gateway -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieve backend credentials [Managed Identity / HTTPS]
* API Gateway -> Azure Application Insights: Forward telemetry and W3C Trace Context headers [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Azure API Management & Azure Front Door: Chosen for WAF protection, rate-limiting, and native routing policies.
* Azure App Configuration: Stores version-controlled routing rules to support rapid one-day fallback (R-06).
* Azure Key Vault: Secures mainframe credentials and API keys via Managed Identities.
* Bicep / Terraform: Infrastructure as Code for automated, drift-free deployments.
* Azure Application Insights: Provides distributed tracing and observability.

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict security boundaries while abstracting legacy complexity to meet strict data consistency and performance mandates. It specifically accommodates the team's low cloud experience through managed Azure services and externalized configuration.]

Claims Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
[A hybrid cloud platform gradually modernizing a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims system while maintaining business continuity.]

## Key Elements
- Claims Web Application (React SPA / Azure App Service)
- BFF Routing & Session Controller (Node.js/Express)
- Claim Workspace UI (React/TypeScript)
- Local State & Sync Manager (IndexedDB / Workbox / Web Crypto API)
- Client-Side Validation & Mapping Engine (TypeScript / Zod)
- Telemetry & Error Boundary Component (React / OpenTelemetry Web)
- External Systems: Microsoft Entra ID, API Gateway, Legacy Mainframe

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Claims Web Application: HTTPS/REST
- Claim Workspace UI -> BFF Routing & Session Controller: HTTPS/REST
- BFF Routing & Session Controller -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST
- Claim Workspace UI -> Client-Side Validation & Mapping Engine: In-memory TS

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Unified hosting for React SPA and Node.js BFF to minimize operational complexity for cloud-novice teams.
- React / TypeScript: Modern UI framework supporting WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility and rapid adjuster workflows.
- Web Crypto API & IndexedDB: Client-side storage with encrypted payload caching to handle intermittent connectivity.
- Azure App Configuration: Dynamic feature flagging for rapid claim-type migration and one-day switch-backs.
- OpenTelemetry & Application Insights: Distributed tracing and proactive health monitoring across hybrid lag.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture securely accelerates claims processing and phased migration while protecting legacy data constraints and minimizing operational overhead for a cloud-novice team.]

Audit & Reporting Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
This system is an Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system while maintaining business continuity. It provides a secure, cloud-hosted web application and audit dashboard alongside the legacy system during a three-year hybrid migration phase.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Compliance Officers / Auditors
- Claims Team Leads
- Legacy Mainframe System of Record (COBOL/DB2, On-Premises)
- Insurer Active Directory / Entra ID
- API Gateway (Azure Front Door / Azure API Management)
- Claims Web Application (React / Azure App Service)
- Audit & Reporting Dashboard (React / Azure App Service)
- Reporting API Component (.NET 8 Web API / Azure App Service)
- Dashboard UI Component (React / TypeScript)
- Audit Trail Logger Component (.NET 8 / Azure Functions)
- Alerting & Notification Component (.NET background worker / Azure Functions)
- Export Worker Component (.NET 8 Isolated Worker / Azure Function)
- Claims Core Service (Node.js/TypeScript on Azure Container Apps)
- Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sync Worker (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions / .NET)
- Read-Model DB (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Azure Blob Storage (WORM-enabled)
- Enterprise Notification System

## Relationships
- Dashboard UI -> Reporting API: Queries audit logs and KPI metrics [HTTPS / REST, JWT Bearer]
- Reporting API -> Read-Model DB: Reads denormalized audit and reporting views [TCP / TLS]
- Reporting API -> Enterprise Notification System: Dispatches threshold alerts [HTTPS / REST]
- Export Worker -> Azure Blob Storage: Writes immutable reports and generates SAS download links [HTTPS, Azure SDK]
- Audit & Reporting Dashboard -> Identity Provider (Entra ID): Single Sign-On (SSO) [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts React frontend and .NET 8 Web API for managed scalability and zero-downtime blue/green deployments.
- Azure Functions (.NET 8): Powers asynchronous export and alerting workers with low infrastructure overhead.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Stores denormalized read-models for low-latency reporting queries.
- Azure Blob Storage: Provides WORM-compliant immutable storage for audit logs and report exports.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages asynchronous message queuing and export job distribution.
- React / TypeScript: Renders responsive adjuster and compliance user interfaces.
- Bicep / Terraform: Automates infrastructure provisioning to mitigate team cloud-inexperience risks.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe modifications while leveraging managed Azure PaaS services to ensure fast screen loads and strict data consistency. This approach minimizes operational risk for an inexperienced cloud team while guaranteeing regulatory compliance, audit immutability, and seamless claim migration.

[The system is a modern hybrid Claims Platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system while maintaining uninterrupted processing. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster management while ensuring zero data loss and seamless 3-year migration.]

## Key Elements
- Users: Policyholders, Brokers, Claims Adjusters
- External Systems: Legacy Mainframe System of Record, Insurer Active Directory (Entra ID), Enterprise Notification System
- Containers: API Gateway (Azure Front Door / Azure API Management), Claims Web Application (React / Azure App Service), Audit & Reporting Dashboard (React / Azure App Service), Claims Core Service (Node.js/TypeScript on Azure Container Apps), Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sync Worker (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions / .NET)
- Components (Claims Core Service): Command Router & Validation Component, Aggregate Root & Business Logic Engine, Event Store Repository (Azure Cosmos DB), Outbox Publisher Worker, Saga & Compensation Coordinator

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Claims Core Service: Dynamic routing of requests [gRPC / HTTPS with mTLS and JWT]
- Claims Core Service -> Legacy Mainframe System: Hybrid data sync [MQ/AMQP and mTLS over IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute]
- Claims Core Service -> Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sync Worker: Event streaming [AMQP via Azure Service Bus]
- Command Router -> Aggregate Root: Dispatches validated commands [In-memory]
- Aggregate Root -> Event Store Repository: Appends immutable domain events [HTTPS via Azure Cosmos DB SDK]
- Event Store Repository -> Outbox Publisher: Streams uncommitted events [Database Change Feed]
- Outbox Publisher -> Saga Coordinator: Triggers compensation flows on integration failure [Async callback]
- Saga Coordinator -> Azure Service Bus (DLQ): Routes failed business events [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / TypeScript: Core runtime for Claims Core Service for rapid development given limited cloud experience.
- Azure Container Apps: Hosting containerized microservices with built-in revision management for canary deployments.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Event store persistence with customer-managed keys (CMK) for immutability and zero data loss.
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event messaging and Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for reliable claim processing.
- Azure Key Vault: Centralized secret management and envelope encryption for PII/financial event payloads.
- Bicep / Terraform: Automated Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) templates to mitigate team cloud inexperience.
- OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across hybrid boundaries for latency diagnostics.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while using CQRS, Event Sourcing, and Azure Cosmos DB to guarantee zero data loss and sub-second UI performance. It empowers a low-cloud-experience team with managed cloud services, automated IaC, and robust fallback mechanisms to meet strict migration and security constraints.]

Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sy.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a modern hybrid cloud platform that gradually replaces a legacy 30-year-old mainframe claims system while maintaining continuous processing. Its core purpose is to enable incremental claim type migration and fast adjuster user experiences without disrupting core operations.]

## Key Elements
*   [Azure Container Apps (ACA) Background Workers for Integration/Sync Service & Read-Model Sync Worker]
*   [Inbound Event Router component (.NET 8 Isolated Worker)]
*   [Read-Model Projection Engine component]
*   [Legacy Sync Bridge & Mainframe Adapter component]
*   [Azure Service Bus with AMQP protocol]
*   [Azure Cache for Redis for Idempotency Ledger]
*   [Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL read-database]
*   [On-premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe]

## Relationships
*   [Claims Core Service -> Azure Service Bus: Event streaming via AMQP]
*   [Azure Service Bus -> Inbound Event Router: Message consumption via AMQP]
*   [Inbound Event Router <-> Azure Cache for Redis: Deduplication checks via RESP]
*   [Legacy Sync Bridge -> On-premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Bi-directional state synchronization via IPSec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute]
*   [Read-Model Projection Engine -> Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL: Read-model updates]

## Technology Stack
*   [.NET 8 (Isolated Worker model): Chosen for high-throughput messaging and robust dependency injection]
*   [Azure Container Apps (ACA): Chosen over Durable Functions for simpler operations given the team's cloud experience]
*   [Azure Service Bus: Chosen for reliable messaging, sessions, and Dead-Letter Queue support]
*   [Azure Cache for Redis: Chosen for sub-millisecond distributed locking and idempotency checks]
*   [IPSec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute: Chosen for secure, encrypted hybrid connectivity to the on-premise mainframe]

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture insulates adjusters from mainframe latency to meet performance goals while using robust messaging and idempotency controls to prevent data loss. Standardizing on simpler containerized workers matches the team's skill level and ensures reliable, gradual migration.]
